abstract: Tritrophic interactions can have considerable impact on biological control systems, therefore, it is imperative to consider these interactions when implementing or evaluating biological control agents. Crape myrtles, Lagerstroemia indica L. x L. fauriei L., are important non-native ornamental plants from Asia that are widely planted and a major woody landscape species in the southern U.S. Six alkaloids have been identified from L. indica, mostly in the seeds and leaves. Crapemyrtle aphids, Tinocallis kahawaluokalani (Kirkaldy), are host specific to crape myrtle and have been shown to be important prey for many native beneficial insects including coccinellids, mirids, and green lacewings. The crapemyrtle aphids occur in different densities per leaf on crape myrtle cultivars and some native beneficial insects cannot fully develop by feeding solely on these aphids. Moreover, no parasitoids of crapemyrtle aphids are known. This information suggests that plant chemistry is involved in tritrophic interactions between this plant, its herbivores and their natural enemies. The purpose of this study was to investigate the suitability of crapemyrtle aphids as a food source for the green lacewing Chrysoperla rufilabris (Bermeister). Experiments were conducted to test the effects of crapemyrtle cultivar, mature plant height, and source of germplasm on the life history characteristics of C. rufilabris. Crapemyrtle aphids were reared on seven cultivars of crapemyrtle, including Apalachee, Natchez, Sioux, Tuscarora, Lipan, Carolina Beauty, and Byers Wonderful White. Aphids from each cultivar were fed exclusively to green lacewing larvae from egg to adult eclosion. Survivorship by cultivar treatment was determined for developmental stages and growth parameters. Cultivar did not affect larval survival but did affect pupal and total survivorship. Length of pupation was extended by aphids feeding on mid mature height cultivars. Dry mass of larvae and adults were also affected accordingly. Males had lower dry mass than females. Lacewings fed on aphids from tall mature height cultivars developed higher dry mass.

metadata.title: Tritrophic Interactions among Crapemyrtle, Crapemyrtle Aphids, and the Green Lacewing Chrysoperla rufilabris (Burmeister)

summary: Tests whether crapemyrtle aphids reared on different crapemyrtle cultivars support development and survival of the green lacewing Chrysoperla rufilabris.
title: Tritrophic Interactions among Crapemyrtle, Crapemyrtle Aphids, and the Green Lacewing Chrysoperla rufilabris (Burmeister)
